p: It is stated in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 6, 22a):
"Rather, they all cry out in prayer
The intent is along the lines of what they said
Now as for the Tikkunim disparaging this —
seemingly the statement of the Gemara (Bava Basra ibid.)
who said to Rebbi, "Sustain me like a dog,"
so as not to benefit himself
through the honor of the Torah,
However, certainly a person should not
that he is among those who dwell in the house of Hashem
all the days of his life,
and has no connection at all
with the needs of this world.
אֲבָל גַּם לֹא יַפְרִיז עַל הַמִּדָּה
But neither should he go to the other extreme
of placing all his hope and aim
solely on the needs of his body.
This is what the Tikkunim disparage —
that they "cry out like dogs, 'Give, give'";
even if there rests upon a person
the yoke of earning a living,
he should hope in his soul and yearn
to merit being among those who dwell in the house of Hashem.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר הָרַבִּי רַבִּי בּוּנֶם מִפְּשִׁיסְחָא
As the Rebbe, Reb Bunim of Peshischa,
that David HaMelech, peace be upon him,
to be among those who dwell in the house of Hashem;
rather, this itself is what he asked
of Hashem Yisbarach — that there be
that at least this would be
"my dwelling in the house of Hashem
all the days of my life," etc.
From here to the end is from his holy manuscript:
On Rosh Hashanah we are judged
and so too all the additions
And sustenance — as they said in Beitzah (16a):
"For it is a statute for Yisrael," etc. —
and on the first Rosh Hashanah
of the world's creation man was created
and life was put into him,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (בְּרֵאשִׁית ב, ז) וַיִּפַּח וְגוֹמֵר.
as it says (Bereishis 2:7), "And He blew," etc.
"And He blessed," etc., "Be fruitful and multiply," etc.
(And there (verse 30) it says, "And it was so,"
for that is when it became food;
and not the utterance "Be fruitful and multiply,"
that the "And He said"s of Creation were nine.
"And He said, Be fruitful and multiply,"
for then the power of procreation was given;
and this is the ninth utterance,
which corresponds to the attribute of Yesod.
for the whole judgment of Rosh Hashanah
is by the weighing of merits,
"the intermediate are held in suspense," etc.;
וַהֲרֵי אָמְרוּ סוֹף מוֹעֵד קָטָן (כח, א)
Yet they said at the end of Moed Katan (28a):
But it is known what is said in the Zohar
סוֹף פָּרָשַׁת אַחֲרֵי (חֵלֶק ג עט, ב)
at the end of Parshas Acharei (Zohar III 79b)
that children depend on the holy Mazala,
As is known, the four letters
and Arich Anpin, which is Atika Kadisha,
is alluded to in the tip of the Yud,
And likewise in man, who is called "in Our image,"
there are the brain and the heart,
the two arms and the legs,
these are the instruments of action —
and the mouth, which is speech;
they correspond to the nine attributes, as is known,
and this is graspable to man.
And "Mazala" is the name for the root of the soul,
which is not graspable to the person himself,
אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִינְהוּ לָא חָזוּ
